EMMET provides an environment to existing interface developers which supports the exploration and evaluation of speech and gesture interface designs without requiring the developers to have an understanding of the implementation details of speech or gesture processing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EMMET has been developed as a tool for multimodal interface design.

EMMET provides an environment for user interface development which supports speech and gesture as first class input modalities, allows developers to quickly distribute their prototypes over the web, and provides developers with the ability to receive usage statistics collected remotely.

the development of the EMMET toolkit has allowed us to realize the following: (1) the integration of speech and gesture recognition into an existing user interface toolkit (2) the ability to quickly distribute multimodal interface prototypes through the Web (3) a mechanism to easily collect usage statistics remotely for each use of the prototype (4) the realization that multimodal interfaces can be developed and deployed in a relatively simple manner (5) the realization of a number of design guidelines for speech and gesture based user
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of EMMET is a step in the direction of making speech and gesture modal input as ubiquitous as the conventional modalities.
the development of a tool such as EMMET is a worthwhile endeavor as it allows interface designers to easily explore the design of speech and gesture interfaces.
